title: How ChatGPT Works
hook: ChatGPT has no idea what it's saying.

sections.narration: ChatGPT has no idea what it's saying. Seriously. It's doing one thing, over and over: guessing the next word. Here's the whole trick, in one minute.
sections.visual: A chat window: a user asks something, the reply appears word by word, then the animation freezes and shows the model choosing between candidate next words with percentages.

sections.narration: Step one: your message gets chopped into tokens. Not words — chunks. Watch: chatgpt becomes two tokens. And every token is turned into a long list of numbers, because neural networks only speak math.
sections.visual: A sentence splits into colored token chips; 'chatgpt' visibly splits into 'chat' + 'gpt'; each chip pours a small column of numbers below it.

sections.narration: Step two: those numbers flow up through a transformer — a giant stack of layers where every token looks at every other token and asks: who matters for what comes next? That's the famous attention mechanism.
sections.visual: 3D: glowing token dots below a translucent stack of layers; a web of attention lines connects every token to every other; a spark rises through the stack; slow camera orbit.

sections.narration: Step three: out comes a probability for every possible next token. The capital of France is... Paris, ninety-two percent. It picks one, sticks it on the end, and runs the whole loop again. That's it. And notice — it ranks likely words. It never checks facts. That's exactly why it can be confidently wrong.
sections.visual: Prompt with a blank; a ranked bar chart of candidate words with probabilities; Paris wins and flies into the blank; a loop arrow labeled 'repeat'; warning caption about facts.

sections.narration: So that was the ten-thousand-foot view. Coming up in this series: tokenizers — why AI can't spell. Embeddings — how meaning becomes math. And attention — the hundred-billion-dollar idea.
sections.visual: Three episode cards slide in: EP2 Tokenizers, EP3 Embeddings, EP4 Attention, each with a one-line teaser.

sections.narration: Follow so you don't miss episode two.
